variety: Numbers are identical in Argentina and Mexico, so either female voice may read them. Argentine accent is welcome but not required.
pronunciation_note: English-style respelling, capitals mark the stressed syllable. Argentine accent: "ll" and "y" sound like "sh".

phrases.when: Written with c, but it sounds like an s: the c before i is soft.
One syllable, like “say” plus s. Do not stretch it into two.
Two syllables, not three. Do not mix it up with seis: siete has the t.
The ch sounds like the ch in “chair”: OH-choh, stress on the first syllable.

hook: Count from five to eight in Spanish. Four words.
outro: Say them out loud. Nine and ten are next.
